questions.question: What should you do when riding at night?

options.text: Ride faster.
Stay farther behind other vehicles.
Ride closer to other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther behind other vehicles.
questions.explanation: At night, ride slower and stay farther behind other vehicles. Use the headlights of cars ahead to see the road. Change your lane position as needed when riding at night.

questions.question: How should you stop your motorcycle during a normal stop?

options.text: Use only the front brake.
Use the front and rear brakes at the same time.
Use only the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the front and rear brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: During a normal stop, use both the front and rear brakes at the same time. Then downshift.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Vehicles will enter the road ahead.
A signal is coming.
Come to a full stop, then go when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a full stop, then go when safe.
questions.explanation: Red octagonal signs are stop signs. You must come to a complete stop. Look for other traffic or pedestrians. Go only when it is safe.

questions.question: If you must both brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, what should you do?

options.text: Do both actions at the same time.
Only brake.
Do one action, then do the other.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action, then do the other.
questions.explanation: If you need to swerve and brake, do them one at a time. Brake first then swerve, or swerve first then brake. Never do both at the same time.

questions.question: How should you secure a load on your motorcycle?

options.text: Secure it as low as possible.
Secure it as high as possible.
Attach it to a sissy bar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Secure it as low as possible.
questions.explanation: If you carry a load without saddlebags, secure it as low as possible. Do not attach loads to a sissy bar because it raises the center of gravity and makes the motorcycle less stable.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT important for helmet protection?

options.text: Meeting U.S. DOT standards.
Being loose-fitting.
Having no damage.

questions.correctAnswerText: Being loose-fitting.
questions.explanation: A good helmet must meet U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards, fit snugly, and have no cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps. A loose-fitting helmet does not provide good protection.

questions.question: What should you do when riding over grooved pavement in a work zone?

options.text: Look down to watch the road surface.
Keep your head and eyes up.
Move to the edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your head and eyes up.
questions.explanation: Keep your head and eyes up in a work zone. Ride slowly over the grooved pavement.

questions.question: What is the minimum following distance for a motorcycle under normal conditions?

options.text: Two seconds.
Three seconds.
Four seconds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two seconds.
questions.explanation: Keep at least two seconds between you and the vehicle ahead under normal conditions. Use a larger distance when conditions are poor.

questions.question: What should you do if your front wheel locks while braking?

options.text: Release the front brake right away, then apply it again.
Release the front brake and use only the rear brake.
Keep the front wheel locked until you stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away, then apply it again.
questions.explanation: If the front wheel locks while braking, release the brake immediately and re-apply it.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Right lane ends.
Left lane ends.
Traffic control device ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right lane ends.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions. This sign warns that the right lane will end.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The traffic light will soon turn red.
The traffic light will soon turn green.
Stop and wait for traffic to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: The traffic light will soon turn red.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow light warns you that the light is about to turn red. Slow down and stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection when it turns yellow, keep going.

questions.question: There is usually an oily strip in the center of traffic lanes. Motorcyclists should:

options.text: Stay away from the oil and grease buildup.
Not worry about the oil and grease buildup.
Find the lane with the least oil and grease buildup.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay away from the oil and grease buildup.
questions.explanation: Stay away from oil and grease buildup. The oily strip is usually only two feet wide, so you can often ride on the left or right side of it and still stay in the center part of the lane.

questions.question: When carrying a load on a motorcycle, it should be:

options.text: Secured as high as possible.
Secured as low as possible.
Secured on a sissy bar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Secured as low as possible.
questions.explanation: Keep loads low to protect the motorcycle's balance.

questions.question: What does an integrated braking system do?

options.text: It connects the front and rear brakes together when you apply the rear brake.
It applies the brakes automatically by learning your riding habits.
It connects to the gears and applies the brake when you downshift.

questions.correctAnswerText: It connects the front and rear brakes together when you apply the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Some motorcycles have integrated braking systems that link the front and rear brakes when you press the rear brake pedal. Check your owner's manual for details about your motorcycle's braking system.

questions.question: When positioning yourself on the motorcycle:

options.text: Use your arms to hold yourself up.
Use your arms to steer the motorcycle.
You should have to stretch to reach the handgrips.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your arms to steer the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Position yourself so you use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up. Sit so your elbows are slightly bent when holding the handgrips.

questions.question: What is one difference between goggles and a windshield?

options.text: Goggles protect you from the wind, but a windshield does not.
A windshield protects you from the wind, but goggles do not.
A windshield keeps your eyes from watering better than goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Goggles protect you from the wind, but a windshield does not.
questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes from the wind, but most windshields do not. A windshield alone is not enough—you also need goggles or a face shield.

questions.question: Before starting a turn, a motorcyclist should change gears to:

options.text: Avoid sudden changes in power during the turn.
Keep both hands on the handgrips during the turn.
Keep the motorcycle from slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid sudden changes in power during the turn.
questions.explanation: Change gears before you start to turn. Shifting while turning can cause a sudden power change that makes the rear wheel skid. If you must shift while turning, do it smoothly to avoid skidding.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks up while stopping on a straight road:

options.text: You can usually keep control of the motorcycle.
You will likely lose control of the motorcycle.
You must release the rear brake to regain control.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can usually keep control of the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks while stopping on a straight road, you can leave it locked until you stop completely. A locked rear wheel usually does not affect control if the motorcycle is upright and going straight.

questions.question: The Motorcycle Safety Foundation recommends the SEE strategy for safe riding decisions. What does SEE stand for?

options.text: Search, Evaluate, and Execute.
Slow, Experienced, and Error-free.
Safe, Experienced, and Evasive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Search, Evaluate, and Execute.
questions.explanation: Experienced riders use the SEE strategy to make safe choices while riding. SEE means Search, Evaluate, and Execute.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, a motorcycle responds to turns:

options.text: More slowly than usual.
More quickly than usual.
Normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: More slowly than usual.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds extra weight to the motorcycle. With more weight, the motorcycle responds more slowly to your movements. It takes longer to speed up, slow down, and turn.

questions.question: When passing a vehicle, you:

options.text: May drive 10 mph over the speed limit.
Must not exceed the speed limit.
Must drive faster than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must not exceed the speed limit.
questions.explanation: You must stay within the speed limit when passing. Only pass where it is safe and legal.

questions.question: While riding, you should wear:

options.text: Hearing protection to protect your ears from engine and wind noise.
A helmet to protect your hearing.
A baseball cap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hearing protection to protect your ears from engine and wind noise.
questions.explanation: Engine and wind noise can damage your hearing over time, even with a full-face helmet. Wear hearing protection to prevent this damage.

questions.question: The oily strip down the center of a lane:

options.text: Should only be used if you share the lane with another vehicle.
Usually has good traction, except when it is raining.
Should always be avoided.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually has good traction, except when it is raining.
questions.explanation: The oily strip in the center of the road usually provides enough traction for safe riding, except when wet. The strip is usually narrow, so you can ride on either side of it and still be in the center lane.

questions.question: When motorcyclists ride in a group:

options.text: New riders should lead the group.
New riders should ride near the front of the group.
New riders should ride at the back of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: New riders should ride near the front of the group.
questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should ride near the front, behind the leader. This lets experienced riders lead and watch new riders at the same time.

questions.question: If your front wheel locks while you are braking, you should:

options.text: Keep the tire locked because it helps you stop faster.
Release the front brake and use only the rear brake.
Release the front brake right away and apply it again with control.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away and apply it again with control.
questions.explanation: If the front wheel locks while braking, release the brake pressure immediately. Then re-apply the brake with slow, controlled pressure.

questions.question: Making eye contact with another driver:

options.text: Means they see you.
Does not mean they will yield to you.
Guarantees they will yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not mean they will yield to you.
questions.explanation: Never assume a driver will yield just because you made eye contact. Drivers often look directly at motorcyclists but still fail to see them.

questions.question: Where should you position your motorcycle when entering a curve?

options.text: The outside of the curve
The inside of the curve
Where traffic and road conditions require

questions.correctAnswerText: Where traffic and road conditions require
questions.explanation: Each curve is different. Choose your lane position based on current conditions and adjust as needed.

questions.question: If you accidentally lock your rear brake on dry pavement, you should:

options.text: Release the rear brake.
Keep the rear brake locked until you stop.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the rear brake locked until you stop.
questions.explanation: If the rear wheel locks on dry pavement, leave it locked until you stop. A locked rear wheel will not affect control as long as the motorcycle stays upright and travels straight.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Railroad crossing ahead
Yield
Reduce speed

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing ahead
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions. This sign warns of a railroad crossing ahead.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT affect blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: The amount of alcohol consumed
How fast the alcohol is consumed
How often a person drinks alcohol

questions.correctAnswerText: How often a person drinks alcohol
questions.explanation: BAC is determined by body weight, the amount of alcohol consumed, and how fast it is consumed. The best choice is to never ride after drinking any alcohol.
